subject: Unexpected 429s during heavy bursts — policy alignment & remediation plan
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@heliosai.com>, Helios AI Support <support@heliosai.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected 429s during heavy bursts — initial notice

Hi Alyssa / Helios team,

I wanted to reach out proactively — we observed a series of unexpected 429 responses affecting a subset of requests from HeliosAI between 08:45 and 09:30 PT this morning. The impact manifested as short-lived failures for bursty traffic from a small group of tenants; your job queue shows a ~12% error rate for generation calls during that window.

Immediate notes: 
- We routed additional capacity at 09:02 PT to reduce client-visible errors.
- No data loss or model integrity issues were detected.
- We believe this was caused by a policy translation mismatch between the new burst-window enforcement and your tenant namespace mapping.

Next steps from our side:
1) We will run a targeted config rollback for the burst window rule and monitor for recurrence.
2) Send a short timeline and root-cause hypotheses within 24 hours.
3) Propose a credit for HeliosAI to offset impacted requests while we finalize the postmortem.

Can you confirm if you saw any downstream errors on your side (job retries, degraded user-facing latency) and whether you would like an immediate SRE call?

Apologies for the disruption — we know these errors directly affect end-user experience. I will follow up with more detail once we validate the root cause.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193

Attachment: 429-incident-timeline.csv (summary of aggregated request counts by minute)

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@heliosai.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Greer <tom.greer@heliosai.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s during heavy bursts — initial notice

Thanks for the heads up, Sergio.

We saw elevated retry rates in our ingestion pipeline and a spike in failed backfills for yesterday's batch — most retries recovered but a few timed out which forced manual reruns. Impacted customers reported increased latency for ~10–15 minutes.

Please do an SRE call if you think it will help. We'll also pull logs from our side and share any correlating request ids. We appreciate a credit while you investigate.

Alyssa
Director of Platform Engineering, HeliosAI
alyssa@heliosai.com

---
Forwarded message included below.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s — internal triage notes

Quick internal notes from triage: 
- Root cause: policy-translation service incorrectly interpreted a new burst-window policy leading to double-enforcement for namespaces that matched a legacy alias pattern. In practice, that reduced the apparent quota window for affected tenants.
- Scope: ~18 tenants affected; HeliosAI was one of the heavier impacted customers due to their sustained short bursts.
- Remediation taken: rolled back the new translation at 09:05 PT; added a hotfix to short-circuit double-enforcement checks.
- Next work: persist a mapping integration test, tighten deploy gating for policy translation, add a monitoring alert specifically for sudden increases in 429s attributable to policy mismatch.

Proposed customer-facing language (short): 
"We experienced a brief misconfiguration in our rate-enforcement translation that resulted in unexpected 429 responses for a subset of customers. We rolled back the change and applied a hotfix; we will provide a postmortem and a credit for the impacted request volume."

Marcus, can you confirm the credit amount we should offer (baseline: affected tokens + 20% goodwill)? Marissa, please draft the one-page postmortem and attach the timeline.

Kim

Attachment: policy-diff.patch (diff between expected and deployed translation behavior)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@heliosai.com>, Tom Greer <tom.greer@heliosai.com>, Helios AI Support <support@heliosai.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & remediation offer — HeliosAI (HL-429-20271129)

Hi Alyssa / Tom,

Thank you again for your patience while our team investigated the 429s on 2027-11-29. Below is a concise post-incident summary and the remediation we are proposing.

What happened
- At 08:44 PT on 2027-11-29, a new burst-window enforcement translation deployed to policy-translation service caused an overlap with an existing legacy alias translation. That overlap resulted in double-enforcement for certain tenant namespace patterns and reduced the effective token window, producing unexpected 429 responses for bursty traffic.

What we did
- Immediately rolled back the translation at 09:05 PT and applied a hotfix to stop double-enforcement.
- Restored normal traffic and observed error rates return to baseline within ~6 minutes post-remediation.
- Implemented a protection: deploy gating for translation changes and an automated integration test exercising alias/namespace edge cases.
- Added a dedicated alert that surfaces sudden 429 spikes tied to policy-translation anomalies.

Customer impact
- HeliosAI experienced retries and ~12% failed generation calls between 08:45–09:02 PT; impact window ~17 minutes.
- No user data loss; manual reruns were required for a small percentage of backfills.

Remediation & credit
- We propose a one-time account credit of $4,200 to offset impacted requests and engineering time. Attached is a short credit offer PDF for your records.
- We will also run a joint postmortem review call next week to walk through the timeline and answer any technical questions. Please suggest a few times that work for you.

Follow-ups we will complete by Dec 8:
- Finalized postmortem doc with annotated timeline and exact request IDs (Marissa)
- Deployment gating for policy-translation (Engineering)
- Integration test added to pre-deploy suite (SRE)

If you want us to expedite a compensation change or a larger credit, we can escalate immediately.

Again, sincere apologies for the disruption — this is not the experience we aim to provide. Thank you for raising this promptly; your logs helped accelerate the fix.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Attachment: credit-offer-HeliosAI-20271201.pdf
